question.text: An investor pays Rs. 1,00,000 today and receives Rs. 50,000 at the end of Year 1 and Rs. 60,000 at the end of Year 2. The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: IRR is the rate that makes the present value of inflows equal to the initial outflow: -1,00,000 + 50,000/(1+r) + 60,000/(1+r)^2 = 0. Solving this equation gives r of about 6.39%. Among the listed options, 6.2% is the closest value. The Trap: At 4.6%, PV of inflows = 50,000/1.046 + 60,000/1.046^2 = approximately 47,801 + 54,839 = Rs. 1,02,640, giving an NPV of about positive Rs. 2,640 - not close to zero - so 4.6% is too low. Note: IRR can be approximated by trial and error or computed directly using a financial calculator or spreadsheet IRR function.
